title: Money in that might not be sales
triggerDescription: This money in looks like the director funding the business, a loan, or a returned transfer — not a customer paying you. If that's right, it should not be taxed as revenue, which lowers your bill.

estimatedImpact.basis: Non-sales inflows (director funding, loans, refunds) are not taxable revenue. Confirming them keeps your taxable profit honest — and lower.

title: We can't tell what this payment was for
triggerDescription: Money went out and nothing tells us what for. Pick a category: if it's a real business cost it reduces your taxable profit, but while it stays unknown it cannot be deducted.

estimatedImpact.basis: Categorizing this as a genuine business cost is worth up to ~30% of the amount in tax saved. Unexplained payments save nothing.

title: Tax was already deducted from this payment
triggerDescription: Your customer held back withholding tax from this payment and sent it to the tax office in your name. That money counts against your own tax bill — but only if you collect the credit note and claim it.

estimatedImpact.basis: Assumes the 5% rate for services to Nigerian companies (2024 Withholding Regulations; goods are 2%). Unclaimed WHT is tax paid twice.

title: VAT you may be able to claim back
triggerDescription: This purchase likely included 7.5% VAT. With a valid VAT invoice you can recover that money — and since 2026 the law lets you claim it on services and equipment, not just goods.
evidenceRequired: valid VAT invoice with supplier tax ID, VAT amount, date, invoice number

estimatedImpact.basis: Estimate extracts the 7.5% VAT share from the gross amount. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 widened input-VAT recovery to services and fixed assets — recoverable cash that didn't exist before 2026.

title: Equipment purchase — claim capital allowances
triggerDescription: This looks like equipment you'll use for years (laptop, generator, vehicle, machinery). You don't deduct it all at once — you claim capital allowances every year, and over time that's worth about a third of the price back in tax.
evidenceRequired: VAT-inclusive purchase invoice (VAT charged and paid is a statutory condition for capital allowances under the NTA 2025)

estimatedImpact.basis: Capital allowances under the NTA 2025 First Schedule write the asset off at 10–25% of cost per year (1% held back until disposal). Fully claimed, that's ~34% of the cost saved in CIT plus Development Levy over the asset's life.

title: Salary payments need PAYE records
triggerDescription: These look like salary payments. Keep the payroll schedule and PAYE remittance receipts — they prove the deduction that lowers your profit, and they keep you clear of payroll penalties.

estimatedImpact.basis: Payroll is fully deductible, but only PAYE records prove it if the tax office asks.

title: Big expense with no receipt
triggerDescription: Over ₦1m went out with no invoice or receipt attached. Without evidence the tax office can refuse the deduction — and your tax goes up by roughly a third of this amount.
evidenceRequired: supplier invoice, payroll schedule, or other primary evidence

estimatedImpact.basis: The deduction this expense earns is only as safe as the paperwork behind it.

title: Looks like a failed transfer and its refund
triggerDescription: Equal money out and money in on the same day usually means a transfer failed and bounced back. It isn't income and it isn't a cost — it should sit outside your totals.

estimatedImpact.basis: Counting a bounced transfer as revenue would tax you on money you never earned.

title: Your rates: 30% company tax + 4% levy
triggerDescription: Your turnover is above the ₦100m small-company line, so the standard rates apply: 30% company income tax plus the 4% Development Levy on profits. The way to pay less is to make sure every real cost, allowance and credit is captured here.

estimatedImpact.basis: The 4% Development Levy replaced the TET, IT, NASENI and Police Trust Fund levies. Groups at ₦50bn+ turnover (or in €750m+ multinational groups) also face a 15% minimum effective tax rate.

title: You might qualify for 0% company tax
triggerDescription: Your turnover is at or below ₦100m. If your total fixed assets are also ₦250m or less, the law charges you 0% company income tax and no Development Levy — confirm the fixed-assets box in your company profile to apply it.
evidenceRequired: fixed asset register confirming total fixed assets ≤ ₦250m

estimatedImpact.basis: Small companies (turnover ≤ ₦100m AND fixed assets ≤ ₦250m) pay 0% CIT, 0% CGT and no Development Levy under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.
